subject: Azure marketplace bundling & partner incentive plan
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <procurement@aegisht.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <partner@cloudbridge.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure marketplace bundling + reseller split question

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Procurement at Aegis is preparing the paperwork for an initial 12-month commitment across our Radiology and ClinicalSearch teams. Before we loop legal, we need clarity on two items so we can map to our internal cost center:

1) If we purchase a bundled private offer via Azure Marketplace that includes 2 model SKUs (inference + embedding) under a single PO, can Redwood deliver a single invoice and pass-through partner margin to CloudBridge?
2) We need visibility on the net vs list discounts at three commit tiers (>$250k, >$500k, >$1M ARR). Is there a standard waterfall you use for private offers, or is this negotiated per account?

Can you share a sample pricing spreadsheet and confirm whether partner split is taken off list or net? We want to ensure CloudBridge receives their referral/commission evidence for our procurement flow.

Thanks — if it helps, I can share the PO template tomorrow.

Regards,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Procurement, Aegis HealthTech
Attachment: Aegis_PO_template.pdf (stub)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <procurement@aegisht.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Ellis <partner@cloudbridge.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace bundling + reseller split question

Hi Marta —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes, you can have a single PO/invoice; partner splits are configurable but we recommend applying the partner margin on net-of-discounts to keep marketplace remittances simple.

I'll put Ben and Karthik on the thread to propose a concrete waterfall and a sample private-offer spreadsheet. Jordan, can you confirm CloudBridge's required evidence (invoice flow vs referral confirmation)? Lauren — pinging you for procurement ops notes we may need to call out in the PO template.

I'll follow up with a spreadsheet within the day.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marta Ruiz <procurement@aegisht.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Ellis <partner@cloudbridge.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace bundling + reseller split question

Marta / team —

Attached is a working spreadsheet showing three tiers and how we model list vs net discounts for a bundled private offer. Key points:

- We recommend structuring the bundle as a single Azure private offer SKU that maps to two internal Redwood SKUs (inference compute + embeddings). The private offer shows a single list price with line-item metadata.
- Discount waterfall (example):
  * Tier 1 (> $250k): 15% list discount, partner split 10% of net
  * Tier 2 (> $500k): 20% list discount, partner split 12% of net
  * Tier 3 (> $1M): 25% list discount, partner split 15% of net + small early-commit rebate
- Partner margin is simplest to pay as a percentage of net after the list discount is applied; Azure will still show the private offer list price, but billing remittance is via Redwood -> CloudBridge per the partnership agreement.

I've included a sample line-item layout in the attached: Azure_PO_bundle_pricing.xlsx (stub). Jordan — confirm that CloudBridge is comfortable receiving a monthly invoice + quarterly rebate reconciliation.

Next steps I suggest:
- Stephanie: approve the tier %s and we produce a mutual action plan.
- Marta: if these tiers look reasonable, we'll translate to a private offer (Azure) and provide the DocuSign for signature.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Azure_PO_bundle_pricing.xlsx (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <procurement@aegisht.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Ellis <partner@cloudbridge.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace bundling + reseller split question

Hi all —

Couple of implementation notes from the marketplace/finance side:

- Azure private offers: when you publish a single private-offer SKU mapped to multiple internal SKUs, Azure invoices the customer at the private-offer list price. Redwood issues the customer-facing invoice that reflects the net price after our discount (the PO should reference Redwood's remit instructions).
- Partner remittance: we can handle partner payments two ways — (A) Redwood pays CloudBridge monthly as a % of collected net revenue, or (B) we set a gross-to-net reconciliation cadence (monthly invoice + quarterly batch reconciliation). Option A reduces paperwork for Aegis; Option B is more transparent for audit.
- Evidence & procurement: Jordan, for marketplace audits CloudBridge typically needs a monthly partner statement + a partner addendum to the PO. Marta, if you can include a clause in the PO template that permits Redwood to issue a partner statement, that will unblock procurement.

I propose we lock these items in a mutual action plan:
- Finalize tier discounts (Ben to confirm)
- Map private-offer SKU IDs and invoice flow (Redwood finance)
- Partner payment cadence and evidence (CloudBridge)
- DocuSign signature and initial PO (Aegis)

I can draft the MAP if you want — should be a one-pager.

Karthik
Director, Marketplace Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marta Ruiz <procurement@aegisht.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Thanks — this is helpful. Aegis is comfortable with the waterfall as long as CloudBridge's margin is net-of-discounts and we receive monthly partner statements.

Action items for acceptance:
- Redwood: send the one-page mutual action plan and the private-offer draft (Ben/Karthik)
- CloudBridge (Jordan): confirm monthly partner statement cadence and provide partner addendum language
- Aegis: sign DocuSign once MAP and PO are received — target 11/12 for signature so we can hit a Nov 30 activation date.

Jordan — please send the partner addendum by Monday. Stephanie — please CC finance@redwood.com on the private-offer when you send it.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Procurement, Aegis HealthTech
